## Type of Update

<!-- Select ONE by putting an X in the brackets -->

- [ ] **New instrument** — Add a new instrument to the registry
- [ ] **Identifier correction** — Fix a wrong ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL, FIGI, or LEI
- [ ] **Ticker change** — Record a ticker symbol change
- [ ] **Delisting** — Mark an instrument as delisted
- [ ] **Relisting** — Mark a previously delisted instrument as active
- [ ] **Corporate action** — Add a split, merger, spinoff, or other action
- [ ] **Multi-exchange listing** — Add or update a secondary listing
- [ ] **Metadata correction** — Fix name, sector, industry, or country
- [ ] **Other** — Describe below

## What this template covers

| Section | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| Type of Update | Categorizes the change request |
| Instrument Identification | All known identifiers to locate the instrument |
| Proposed Change | Current vs proposed values |
| Rationale | Why the change is needed |
| Source | Required official source with URL |
| Validation | Self-check before submission |
| Affected Files | Which files need updating |
| Additional Context | Extra information for reviewers |
| Reviewer Checklist | Quality gate for maintainers |

## Why the Source URL is REQUIRED

[Confirmed] Every entry in `identifiers.json` has a `source_url` field. The validator enforces this. Any update without a source will be rejected.

## How this works with the workflow

1. User submits issue using this template
2. Maintainer reviews the source
3. Maintainer applies the change to `identifiers.json`
4. `python3 tools/validate.py` runs
5. `pytest tests/ -v` runs
6. CI validates on push
7. Change is merged

## What NOT to submit

- Ticker changes without an official announcement
- Identifiers without check-digit validation
- Multiple instruments in one issue
- Changes without a source URL
- Speculative additions
